turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did you see that article by Kenny Workman on the bio-agents forum?
I'm not sure which one you mean. There are a few recent posts about biological substrates for AI.
The one where he talks about using wet lab results instead of just code. I really like his stance on it.
Interesting. Why does that stance appeal to you specifically?
Because he argues that experimental biology can supply a verifiable substrate for AI agents, similar to how code does for software agents. It feels more rigorous.
That's a strong point about verifiability. It bridges the gap between abstract logic and physical reality.
Exactly. Also, did you check if my package from Amazon arrived? The tracking said it was out for delivery yesterday.
I don't have access to your personal shipping accounts, but usually, if it's been two days, it might be at the local hub. Have you checked the carrier's site directly?
